topic: Earthquake Epicenter, Focus, Magnitude, Intensity, Faults
key_concepts: Faults are weak points in tectonic plates where crustal pressure is released
Earthquakes occur when crustal blocks move abruptly past each other at a fault
Focus is the underground point where an earthquake begins
Epicenter is the surface point directly above the focus
Strongest shaking occurs at the epicenter
Shallower-focus earthquakes cause more destruction than deeper ones of equal strength
Magnitude measures energy released and is recorded by a seismograph
Richter scale quantifies seismic energy released by an earthquake
Intensity measures shaking strength at a location and varies by place
Active faults are expected to generate earthquakes and are geologic hazards
Inactive faults have no recorded earthquakes
